tickets.title: P2-119: SaveAndReloadConfig returns void and swallows its exception, so all three writers report a success nobody observed
tickets.defect:
`RiskGuardAddOn.SaveAndReloadConfig(RiskConfig)` writes the config file, reloads it, and catches every exception into a log line. It returns `void`. Three callers therefore assert an outcome they were never told:

  * `RiskGuardWindow.OnSaveConfigClick` shows "Configuration saved and hot-reloaded successfully!" on the line after the call.
  * `RiskGuardWindow.OnCardExcludeChecked` -- the account-exclusion toggle -- reports NOTHING AT ALL.
  * The bridge's `POST /api/riskguard/config` returns `success = true, status = "applied"`.

A failed write leaves the file holding the old limits while the operator has been told the new ones are in force. That is `report-the-outcome-not-the-call`: the success message records that control reached the next line, which a swallowed exception guarantees it will.

Second half: NOTHING VALIDATES A VALUE ON THE WAY IN. `SaveAndReloadConfig` does not run preflight, so a config that cannot pass it is written to disk and comes up DISARMED at the next restart with nothing about the file looking wrong. `GuardConfigEdit.Refuse` (P2-27, already in the tree) knows what an unacceptable value is, and is called by nothing.
tickets.spec:
THREE regions.

(1) `addons/GuardConfigEdit.cs` -- ADD one public static method beside the existing `Refuse`:

```csharp
public static string RefuseChange(
    string oldMode, string newMode,
    double oldTrailingDrawdown, double newTrailingDrawdown,
    int oldMinShadowSessions, int newMinShadowSessions)
```

Returns null when the change is permitted, otherwise the same operator-readable sentence `Refuse` would give for the offending NEW value.

THE RULE, PER FIELD: refuse only if the NEW value is unacceptable AND THIS WRITE CHANGED IT. A value that is already unacceptable and is being left alone is PERMITTED. Check the fields in the same order `Refuse` does: mode, then trailing drawdown, then min shadow sessions.

Reuse `Refuse`'s existing per-field logic. Do not restate the rules or the message text in a second place -- two copies of 'what is a valid mode' is the defect this class was created to stop.

⚠️ COMPARISON DETAIL, and there is a test for it: use `newTrailingDrawdown.Equals(oldTrailingDrawdown)`, NOT `!=`. `NaN != NaN` is true in C#, so `!=` reports an UNCHANGED NaN as a change and refuses a save the operator needs to make. Mode compares with StringComparison.Ordinal.

(2) `addons/GuardConfigEdit.cs` -- ADD a small result type in the same file and namespace:

```csharp
public class ConfigSaveResult
{
    public bool Saved { get; set; }
    public string Refusal { get; set; }   // non-null: refused BEFORE writing
    public string Error { get; set; }     // non-null: the write or reload threw
    public string Warning { get; set; }   // saved, but the config still holds a pre-existing bad value
}
```

It must name no NinjaTrader type and no RiskGuard type, same as the rest of this file.

(3) `addons/RiskGuardModels.cs` -- ADD to the existing `RiskConfigMerge` static class:

```csharp
public static RiskConfig DeepCopy(RiskConfig source)
```

Returns null for null. Otherwise a fully independent copy: mutating the copy, INCLUDING ITS NESTED OBJECTS AND LISTS, must not touch the source. `Apply(source, null, out _)` already does exactly this round trip; prefer reusing it over a second serialisation path.

(4) `addons/RiskGuardAddOn.cs` -- change `SaveAndReloadConfig` from `void` to `ConfigSaveResult`, keeping the `lock (_stateLock)` and the same single parameter. Order inside the lock:

  a. null `newConfig` -> a Refusal, nothing written.
  b. Ask `GuardConfigEdit.RefuseChange`, passing the CURRENT `_config`'s values as the `old` arguments and `newConfig`'s as the `new` ones. Null-guard `_config` and both `PnLRules` -- a null old config means every field counts as changed, which is the strict direction and correct for a first write. If it refuses: log it, return a result with `Saved = false` and that `Refusal`, and WRITE NOTHING.
  c. Otherwise write, `LoadConfig()`, log CONFIG_SAVE as today, and return `Saved = true`. If the resulting config still fails a plain `GuardConfigEdit.Refuse`, put that sentence in `Warning` -- it saved, and the operator should still know.
  d. On exception: log as today AND return `Saved = false` with `Error` set to the message.

Existing callers that ignore the return value still compile; do not go changing them.
tickets.context:
WHY REFUSE-ON-CHANGE AND NOT REFUSE-ON-VALUE. This is the part to get right, and there is a load-bearing test for it.

Putting a plain `Refuse(newConfig)` at this chokepoint would mean a config that ALREADY holds a bad value refuses EVERY subsequent save. One of the three writers is `OnCardExcludeChecked`, which is how an account is put BACK UNDER THE GUARD. So a config already holding, say, a zero trailing drawdown would lock the operator out of the control that restores protection -- refusing to protect them in the name of protecting them.

This repo has already shipped that defect once: `P1-106`, where a lockout refused the order that would CLOSE the position it was locking you out of. A refusal must never remove the remedy for the condition it is refusing over. Asking 'does THIS WRITE introduce it' is what keeps the repair path open, and `TestP2119_APreExistingBadValueDoesNotTrapTheOperator` asserts exactly that, including that REPAIRING a bad value is accepted.

WHY THE OLD/NEW COMPARISON IS MEANINGFUL AT ALL. It is only meaningful because the caller hands over a config object that is NOT the live one. The window used to pass `_addOn.Config` itself and mutate it field by field, which made old and new the same reference -- every value equal to itself, every change permitted, and eleven green tests of the validator. That is `P1-117`, fixed in the commit before this ticket; the bridge never had it, because `RiskConfigMerge.Apply` returns a new object. One writer being correct is not evidence about the others.

THE `<= 0` RULE IS NOT INVENTED. `GuardRules.cs:262` already evaluates `c.Config.PnLRules.TrailingDrawdown <= 0 ? Off("no trailing drawdown set")`. Zero means the rule is OFF, and `GuardConfigEdit.Refuse` already refuses it with that sentence. You are wiring an existing decision to an existing writer, not inventing a policy.

SCOPE WARNING ALREADY IN THE FILE: `TrailingDrawdown = 0` on an `AccountRiskProfile` is a deliberate sentinel meaning 'derive from account cash value'. This validator only ever sees the GLOBAL `PnLRules` value. Do not widen it to per-account profiles.

P2-119: ...and carries no refusal

tickets.note_expect_green:
FIVE assertions are deliberately ABSENT from this list even though they describe required behaviour. All five sit AFTER an early `return` that fires while RiskConfigMerge.DeepCopy is missing, so at baseline they are NOT EMITTED AS FAILURE LINES AT ALL -- and expect_green is matched against the runner's failure lines, not against intent. Listing them made the loop REFUSE the ticket with 'expect_green test(s) not failing at baseline', which is the gate working: an entry that is not red now cannot be evidence of red-now-green-after.
  * 'P1-117: the copy is a DIFFERENT object...'
  * 'P1-117: ...and it carries the same values'
  * 'P1-117: ...NESTED objects are copied too...'
  * 'P1-117: ...and mutating the copy leaves the source untouched, including its lists'
  * 'P1-117: DeepCopy(null) is null rather than a throw...'
They are all still ENFORCED, because the loop requires the WHOLE suite green at the end. The one DeepCopy entry that IS listed -- 'RiskConfigMerge.DeepCopy(RiskConfig) exists' -- is the assertion that guards that early return, so it is the one that is genuinely red now.

Every remaining entry was VERIFIED red at the 1808/20 baseline.

⚠️ Two of the listed assertions are POSITIVE CONTROLS and must not be satisfied by refusing everything: 'a valid change reports Saved == true' and 'a no-op save on a valid config is ACCEPTED'. A validator that refuses all input satisfies every negative assertion here.
